claims.text: Conventional preparation of single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically has relatively high porosity.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 has poor resistance to degradation induced by a liquid plating bath.
Residual porosity in ZrB2 leads to micro-holes and eventual component failure during prolonged liquid plating exposure.
Microwave-assisted sintering can densify ZrB2 at a lower temperature than conventional sintering.
Microwave-assisted sintering near 2000 °C can achieve full densification of single-phase ZrB2.
Rapid, volumetric microwave heating produces a uniformly dense ZrB2 microstructure with reduced porosity and enhanced grain-boundary bonding.
Microwave energy directly couples with ZrB2 powders.
Microwave coupling enhances atomic diffusion in ZrB2 at a lower overall processing temperature.
Enhanced diffusion under microwave heating promotes faster densification.
Microwave-assisted sintering minimizes grain growth and pore coalescence in ZrB2.
A consolidated, low-porosity ZrB2 ceramic is less likely to develop micro-holes or degrade during prolonged liquid plating exposure.
Microwave-sintered ZrB2 will have higher density than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Microwave-sintered ZrB2 will have lower porosity and fewer holes than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Microwave-sintered ZrB2 will retain greater mechanical strength and structural integrity during prolonged liquid plating exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
The optimal microwave-sintering temperature and dwell time for ZrB2 have not been fully established.
Scaling microwave processing to large or complex ZrB2 components may introduce additional challenges.
